audience: Owners and operations leaders in established, profitable Sydney service businesses that issue repeatable quotes
problem: A rate or supplier-cost change is updated in one quoting tool but not every template, spreadsheet and sales path, leaving the business with inconsistent prices and late margin checks.
single_message: A price change is not complete until every approved quoting path uses the same version.
supporting_points: Name one approved source for rates, inclusions, GST treatment and quote expiry rules
Push approved changes into quoting paths and flag any legacy template that cannot update
Keep pricing strategy, exceptions, discount authority and unusual scope under human judgement
desired_action: Use the on-site automation review to trace one price change across every quoting path
angle: Turn one approved price change into a controlled update across every quoting path
headline_options: Make every quote use one price
caption_hook_options: A price change is not finished when the spreadsheet is updated.
How many places hold your current price?
One price change should reach every quote.
selected_hook: A price change is not finished when the spreadsheet is updated.
caption_cta: If quote-price drift sounds familiar, the on-site automation review can map one change from approval to every quoting path.

article_outline: Why quote-price drift is an operational problem
Map every quoting path before connecting anything
Create a controlled update and exception path
Keep pricing strategy and commercial judgement human
Test the change with real quoting scenarios
Use an on-site automation review to find the first useful connection

duplicate_review.rejection_reason: Instagram recently used the headline Monday shouldn’t disappear into reporting, making the topic and hook too close.

promotion_hypothesis: Owners recognise inconsistent quoting as a commercial-control problem, while the single-stamp visual makes the one-source principle immediately understandable without hype.
risk_notes: Do not promise margin improvement or invented financial results
